ask: C11, POSIX. progress.c: reusable ANSI progress bar — determinate and indeterminate modes, throughput and ETA estimation with exponential smoothing, terminal width detection via ioctl, carriage-return redraw, and a demo loop over 200 items. write the file.
prose:
`progress.c` is written. Build and run with:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -o progress progress.c -lm
./progress
```

A few things worth noting:

- `pb_draw` re-queries the terminal width on every frame via `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)`, so the bar reflows correctly if you resize the window mid-run.
- The EMA is seeded on the first non-zero interval rather than starting at zero, which avoids a slow ramp-up in the displayed rate after the first item.
- The indeterminate bounce chunk is `bar_w / 4` (minimum 3), so it scales proportionally with terminal width instead of being a fixed pixel count.
- Both `pb_init` and `pb_free` are safe to call on stack-allocated structs — `pb_free` only touches the heap-allocated label copy.

If you want to wire this into a real pipeline, `pb_update` accepts a `delta` so you can call it once per batch rather than once per item, which keeps the EMA more accurate when individual items are very fast.
